title: The Overtime Tax Math Nobody Explains
hook_text: WORKING OVERTIME MIGHT PAY LESS THAN YOU THINK

beats.say: Working that extra 10-hour shift feels like a win, until you run the actual tax math.
beats.visual: A person sitting at a wooden desk under a warm desk lamp, holding a red pen over a blank white notepad.

beats.say: You see that plump paycheck arrive with extra hours logged, and you assume it's pure profit.
beats.visual: Close-up of a hand tapping a smartphone screen displaying a banking app graph.

beats.say: Most workers think bumping up into a higher marginal tax bracket means all their money gets taxed more.
beats.visual: A calculator resting on a dark glass table next to a spilled cup of black coffee.

beats.say: That is the head fake. Only the dollars crossing the bracket threshold face the higher rate.
beats.visual: A pair of reading glasses resting on top of printed financial ledger pages.

beats.say: But why does your net take-home pay on those extra hours still feel surprisingly small?
beats.visual: A close-up shot of hands thumbing through a stack of crisp white tax documents.

beats.say: Here's the math hiding in your payroll stub. Supplemental wages face a flat withholding rate.
beats.visual: A computer keyboard shot from a low angle with soft window light casting long shadows.

beats.say: Employers often withhold 22% federally for bonuses or overtime chunks right off the top.
beats.visual: A silver fountain pen resting beside a blank checkbook on a dark oak table.

beats.say: Add state taxes and payroll deductions, and that bonus hour yields a noticeably lower effective bonus.
beats.visual: A person's silhouette standing by a tall glass window looking out at a rainy evening city.

beats.say: You didn't take a pay cut, but your hourly yield shrank because of upfront withholding rules.
beats.visual: An overhead shot of coins scattered next to a heavy brass desk stapler.

beats.say: Now you know how the brackets work. Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: A hand closing a leather-bound journal against a dark textured background.

caption: The math behind overtime withholding often surprises your bank account. #Overtime #Taxes #PersonalFinance #MoneyTips #Paycheck
description: Breaking down marginal tax brackets and supplemental wage withholding to show why extra hours sometimes yield a smaller effective bonus than expected.
first_comment: Did your last overtime check feel smaller than you expected?

facts.claim: Supplemental wages like bonuses and certain overtime amounts have a flat federal withholding rate of 22% in the US.
facts.basis: IRS Publication 15 (Circular E), Employer's Tax Guide.

loop_map.stakes: A paycheck with extra overtime hours logged.
